summary: Intermittent streaming timeouts during peak bursts — soft 429 queueing misread as backend hang
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent long-tail streaming timeouts (client reports 'no data for 10s' and connection closes) during high-volume bursts. Impact: Several production customers on Dedicated capacity (AcuityAI) observed elevated tail latency and perceived model hangs that correlate with spikes in concurrent requests. Customer interpreted as model slowdown/serving regression.

Hypothesis: Initial triage indicates not a model regression but a server-side soft-throttle pacing window combined with synchronous client retries. When many clients simultaneously retry on 429 responses with minimal jitter and high concurrency, requests queue inside the serving runtime token buffer and batching window, causing long head-of-line delays and stream connection timeouts.

Desired outcome: Restore predictable streaming responsiveness and provide clear guidance to customer SDKs to avoid retry amplification. Implement short-term mitigations and a durable fix on the rate-limiter and SDK behavior.
impact: AcuityAI reports 8% of streaming sessions experienced disconnects or timeouts during hourly spikes; business impact includes degraded product UX and increased support support volume.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Using dedicated tenant for AcuityAI in prod/us-east, fire 1,200 concurrent warm streaming requests to /v1/streams with default SDK concurrency settings (64).
2) Induce a quota soft-exhaustion by sustaining token-heavy prompts for ~30s (average request length 350 tokens).
3) Configure client-side retries to immediate exponential backoff (base 50ms) without randomized jitter.

4) Observe: server returns ephemeral 429s with soft-throttle header; clients retry synchronously; within 10-15s overall observed streaming initiation rate drops and many streams time out on client side.
investigation_notes: 03/10 03:12 UTC: Support received first customer alert (AcuityAI SLO-based health check).

03/10 03:18 UTC: Confirmed error spikes on tenant: increased 429s and elevated request queue depth in the serving-runtime metrics (trace link: https://grafana.redwood/v/stream-queue?orgId=1&var-tenant=acuityai).
03/10 03:25 UTC: Correlation observed between 429 burst windows and client retry bursts from AcuityAI IP block (Netflow: 35.193.*.*).

03/10 03:40 UTC: Profiling of serving-runtime shows large per-tenant pacing bucket with refill tick aligned to 1s window. Head-of-line blocking increases mean time-to-first-token when queue length > 200.
03/10 04:05 UTC: Client SDK behavior (AcuityAI using SDK v1.3.1) retries with low jitter and concurrency defaults of 64, amplifying queued requests.
root_cause: Soft 429 pacing window configured for per-tenant fairness plus aggressive client-side retry logic from customer SDKs without jitter. The synchronized refill and high concurrency cause large transient queueing in the serving runtime which manifests as long-tail streaming timeouts. Not a model quality regression.
mitigation_steps_taken: 03/10 04:20 UTC: Applied temporary tenant-level emergency soft-throttle policy change: reduced per-tenant pacing window from 1s -> 200ms for AcuityAI to reduce queue headroom.

03/10 04:35 UTC: Support advised AcuityAI to immediately roll out SDK config change: lower concurrency to 8 and enable randomized jitter on retries. Customer applied change and reported immediate improvement in observed timeouts.
03/10 05:10 UTC: Server-side added 'Retry-After' and 'x-rw-remaining' headers to 429 responses for better client guidance (rolled to prod us-east only for canary tenants).
resolution: Partial fix deployed: pacing window tuned for affected tenant and 429 headers improved. Customer SDK guidance provided and AcuityAI updated client config. Full mitigation requires runtime rate-limiter change and SDK release. Issue remains In Progress until SDK rollout and global runtime change complete.
postmortem_actions: 1) Engineering: implement staggered per-tenant refill (randomized micro-ticks) to prevent global refill alignment (owner: Priya Patel, ETA: 2026-03-18).
2) SDK: release v1.4.3 with default retry jitter enabled, lower default max concurrency to 16, and built-in 429-aware backoff (owner: DevX team, ETA: 2026-03-15).
3) Docs: update 'Handling 429s' guidance in Redwood SDK docs and add runbook steps for customer support (owner: Docs, ETA: 2026-03-12).
4) Observability: add tenant-level anomaly alert for sustained queue depth > 150 for more than 30s (owner: SRE, ETA: 2026-03-13).

notes_for_support: If customers report 429s as 'model hang', confirm client SDK retry configuration (concurrency and jitter) and check serving-runtime queue depth. Use canary tool to temporarily lower per-tenant pacing window while Engineering implements refill de-synchronization.
follow_up: Track SDK release v1.4.3 and server PR. After releases, schedule a post-incident review and finalize runbook. Notify affected customers and update KB article with concrete SDK examples and recommended defaults.
